acceptanceCriteria.statement: One pipeline: the storm slice has ONE definition, under src/, that both front-ends import. Driver pack #10 `src/worldengine/drivers/stormDeck.js` exports `stormDeckPack(condition, ctx) -> { drivers, attributes, meta }`, `STORM_DECK_ENTRY` (predicate character-identical to polarDeck's: compositionClass === 'gas'; gates ['greatSpot','stormTrain']), the colour law (the lab's `_stormColor`: chromophore age ramp, 20 % deck tint, barge/scooter/dark-spot branches, as NAMED coefficients), the deck-height law (`_stormDeckZ` over STORM_DECK), the slot composer (`composeStormSlots`: slot 0 = primary iff gate, train iff gate, cap 8, aux slot-synced, count = written) and the lab mirror (`STORM_LAB_BINDING` + `stormDeckLabState`). The lab imports them back and its own copies are deleted: `applyStormState` no longer calls `resolveStormE` itself, and `_stormColor`, `_stormDeckZ` and the hand-written slot loop are gone from world-engine-lab.html. Pack #1's fence comment stays TRUE (giantDeck still emits no uStorm* name) and polarDeck's source-scan fence stays green (it still never names resolveStormE / writeStormESphere / bakeStormEAttributes).

verifyVia.input: Static: grep the lab for the deleted definitions and for the import-back line; grep giantDeck.js / polarDeck.js for the fenced names; run tests/driver-pack-polardeck.test.js and tests/driver-pack-giantdeck.test.js unchanged; assert STORM_DECK_ENTRY is in PACKS by IDENTITY and that stormDeck is pack #10 (giantSurface holds #8, fluvialDeck #9).
verifyVia.observable: Deny-scan clean (0 hits for the three lab-local definitions and for a lab-side `resolveStormE(` call outside the import); the import line present; both sibling suites green byte-for-byte; the registry membership fence in drivers/index.js passes with the new entry and the emitted-name sets of every pre-existing pack are unchanged (asserted as SET MEMBERSHIP over real pack outputs on the corpus, not as counts).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The pack contract learns exactly ONE new value shape and nothing already on it moves. `resolveDriver` admits an array of equal-length numeric arrays (every component finite; ragged or non-numeric throws PackContractError) and `writePackUniforms` writes such a value slot-wise through each target element's `.set(...)`, throwing when the target array's elements are not settable. Every driver every existing pack emits — over the 24-seed corpus (124 solid + 32 gas bodies) and the 18 driver presets — resolves to a value identical before and after the change, and stormDeck is the ONLY pack that emits the nested shape.

verifyVia.input: Headless: capture every pack's resolved driver map on every corpus body and preset at the parent commit (a fixture), re-run at HEAD, deep-compare; scan all pack outputs for nested arrays; feed the writer a nested driver aimed at a scalar uniform, at a ragged array, and at an array of plain numbers [CONTROL — each must throw].
verifyVia.observable: Zero drivers differ (by value, not by count); the nested-shape scan names exactly stormDeck; the three controls throw PackContractError with the stated reasons; the five uStorm* uniforms on a gas material hold Vector4/Vector3 instances after the write (instanceof, so the element-wise overwrite defect is falsifiable).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Refactor byte-identity under the LAB's policy. For every driver preset × the pinned (macroSeed, stormSeed) grid, the pack's mirror `stormDeckLabState` reproduces every state field `applyStormState` wrote before the change (spotStrength/Center/Radius/Rot/Aspect/Mode/Color/Companion/Age/Emboss/Billow, trainStrength, trainSpots[] with every member field, trainCount, _stormUranian) deep-equal to a fixture captured from the lab BEFORE the change, and `composeStormSlots` reproduces the lab's per-frame uniform writes byte-for-byte under all four checkbox combinations. Measured on the same CONDITION object, not the same preset name. Any deviation (the candidate is the T_eq fallback: the lab read `_fp.T_eq ?? 288`, the pack reads `condition.T_eq`; all 17 presets define T_eq so the expectation is zero) is RECORDED as a declared deviation in this contract, never absorbed.

For every gas body in the corpus, `stormDeckPack(cond, ctx).meta.vortices` deep-equals the `vortices` list returned by `bakeStormEAttributes` when called with pack #1's OWN `meta.e5Drivers` + composition + T_eq at (labMacroSeed, GAME_STORM_SEED) — two independent derivations of the input chain, one writer — and `meta.count` equals giantDeck's `meta.stormCount` on every gas body. Solid bodies: the registry never applies the pack, and calling it directly emits nothing (the polarDeck idiom).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every gas body gets its storm family from its condition, and no two are the same world. Over the 24-seed corpus (32 gas bodies) RECORD per body: regime, T_eq, vigor, primary role/mode, train family, count, primary lat/lon, hot-Jupiter and Uranian flags; RECORD the distribution against the scoping read (26 warm / 6 dark primaries; 22 pearl trains / 4 barge+oval / 6 scooter families; counts 2–7; 19 sub-Neptune / 6 Saturnian / 7 Neptunian; 0 hot-Jupiter, 0 Uranian). PIN only the distinctness floor: ≥ 20 distinct primary latitudes and ≥ 20 distinct longitudes over the 32 (a constant seed collapses both to 1). Seed identity: mounting the same body twice yields identical slots; two gas bodies of one system differ.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: MAX'S GATE (deferred-to-max, never agent-PASSed). Flying in on a gas giant in a procedural system with the `I` key: do the great spot and its storm family read as PART of the gas deck — riding its bands, the bands wrapping around them — in the same place when he comes back; and does the next gas giant carry a different family? He judges the WIRE: "driven by the new system", not "rolling dice", not "in the same place every seed". The great spot "does not blend correctly with the rest of the gas" (QB-16) and the missing "ink in water" complexity (QB-18) are logged lab defects deferred by his 2026-09-02 ruling — visible here, and not this gate.
